title: Coursebook backend RPC v26
description: v26 is one additive amendment over v25 (CP-052, the plate's own route geometry): the `world_brief` record gains one optional array, `route_anchors`, an ordered list of `{anchor_id, section_id, x, y}` entries whose `x`/`y` are normalised 0–1 coordinates of a section on the plate box, so `world.read` returns a plate manifest the course home already renders instead of refusing it. The array is presentation geometry, not instruction: it carries no check, answer key, rubric or attempt, and it never changes a plate's prompt, its content-addressed cache key or any lesson hash. A brief that declares no anchors keeps its exact v25 shape and bytes. A malformed anchor is refused at the field, never by a generic internal error. No method, request shape, required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves; `contracts/rpc.v25.json` stays byte-identical history and `x-supersedes` names it. v25 is one additive amendment over v24 (CP-005, the shelf and card facts): the `library_item` record gains seven required properties — `sections_done`, `sections_total`, `checks_recorded`, `is_new`, `subject_label`, `cover_artifact_id` and `last_studied_at` — so a v3 card renders every number, chip and cover from one `library.list` read and the UI never computes or invents one. `sections_done`/`sections_total` are the current plan's objective count and its independent-evidence count; `checks_recorded` counts the distinct checks this enrollment has a committed attempt for; `is_new` is true only when the enrollment has no attempt at all; `subject_label` is the course's declared subject domain, else null; `cover_artifact_id` is the approved world's cover artifact, else the pack's declared cover artifact, else null; `last_studied_at` is the latest attempt the enrollment recorded, else null. There is deliberately no rating, no learner count and no percentage. No method, request shape, existing required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves; `contracts/rpc.v24.json` stays byte-identical history and `x-supersedes` names it. v24 is one composed additive amendment over v23: GM-007's four away-from-screen `homework.*` methods, GM-018's `takehome.html`, and this GM-004 World Studio part. GM-004 appends the four `world.*` methods frozen by GM-001 in `coursebook/gm_contract.py` (world.read, world.style.preview, world.generate, world.approve) together with the documented extra `course.mode.set`, and `course.create` gains one optional `presentation_mode` field so a new course records Game intent at creation. World plates are textless orientation art; the read never generates art and never writes the mode. A style choice and a final kit approval are two separate hash-fenced facts. The composed document declares 93 methods. No v1-v23 method, request shape, required key, error code, job kind or vocabulary value moves; `contracts/rpc.v23.json` stays byte-identical. v24 appends one additive method (GM-018, take-home print follow-ups): `takehome.html` returns the stored take-home pack as a self-contained, selectable-text HTML document that shares the PDF page composition — the learner page for a learner pack, plus the parent guide and the separate parent-only answer guide for a parent pack. The document carries the document title, its language, escaped text, no scripts, no images and no external fetch; a captioned plate keeps its text alternative as an accessible region label. It is returned as content, not as a second download handle: `artifact.get` remains the only download handle, and HTML is never adopted into the artifact store. No method, request shape, required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves; `rpc.v23.json` stays byte-identical history and `x-supersedes` names it. v24 is v23 with one additive amendment (GM-007, away-from-screen homework): four methods are appended, `homework.create`, `homework.read`, `homework.complete` and `homework.skip`. `homework.create` proposes one task with one target, one context, one observable success criterion and 3-10 minutes, sourced from the lesson's authored away-from-screen block; it refuses a generic duration card, multiple targets, surveillance and graded completion with `POLICY_VIOLATION` and a named `details.reason`. `homework.read` returns the task, its append-only event trail and a one-page sheet with its cited sources. `homework.complete` records `self_reported_done` or `parent_reported_done` and `homework.skip` records an honest skip; neither writes an attempt, transition, evidence, engagement or mastery row, and a parent-reported task is never independent verification. Homework is not a course, not a chat thread and never an external send. No v1-v23 method, request shape, required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves; `rpc.v23.json` stays byte-identical history and `x-supersedes` names it. v23 is v22 with GM-005's take-home family. v23 is v22 with one additive amendment (GM-005, Parent Studio take-home packs): six methods are appended, `takehome.sources`, `takehome.preview`, `takehome.create`, `takehome.approve`, `takehome.export` and `takehome.read`. `takehome.sources` lists the learner courses and imported packs a parent may draw from, with section/objective/lesson preview and parent-only authoring courses excluded unless explicitly shared. `takehome.preview` composes the proposed pages. `takehome.create` mints a draft bound to the source course, objective, lesson version and content hash; `takehome.approve` approves the actual pages; `takehome.export` renders the A4/Letter print artifact; `takehome.read` returns the pack with the learner page and the answer guide as separate page objects. The source course, lesson, evidence and attempts are never written, and a pack edit invalidates only the pack. No existing method, required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves. v22 is v21 with one additive Game Mode implementation amendment (GM-011, the lesson-bound tutor): `tutor.ask` and `tutor.history` are appended. Wire contract for the Coursebook backend. v22 is v21 with one additive Game Mode implementation amendment (GM-011, the lesson-bound tutor): two methods are appended, `tutor.ask` and `tutor.history`. `tutor.ask` answers one learner question inside a thread bound to a lesson run, with a bounded context envelope that excludes answer keys, checks, rubric and attempts, no tools, and citations that must resolve to a lesson block id or a course source id. While a check is open the final answer is withheld and the response names the assist policy; the command never writes an attempt, transition or evidence row, and a provider failure is a named state (`provider_failure`) rather than an empty answer. `tutor.history` reads the persisted thread for one lesson run. Tutor turns are excluded from pack and course export and are never graded. No existing method, required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves. v21 is v20 with the first additive Game Mode implementation amendment (GM-009, the game-only engagement layer): two methods are appended, `engagement.read` and `engagement.award`. `engagement.read` is the Game header read model (xp total, cosmetic level, `Game progress` labelled play progress, bounded recent events) and is refused outside a `game` course; `engagement.award` appends one XP event idempotently per `(enrollment_id, action_kind, action_id)` and refuses any action id that is not a real recorded action. No existing method, required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves, and engagement is never joined by an evidence, parent, pack or export read. The remaining Game Mode method names stay frozen in `coursebook/gm_contract.py` and land with their own handlers. v20 is v19 with one additive amendment (H-194b, the read seam the H-194 UI needs): `parent.blueprint.read` gains one required response array, `sections`, one entry per composed section carrying `section_id`, `objective_id`, `ordinal`, `title`, `lesson_state`, `lesson_version` and `page_hash`. `page_hash` is the exact digest `lesson.revise` fences on, so the desktop can call `lesson.revise`/`lesson.regenerate` for a section that has never been revised. No method is added or moved, no request shape changes, no error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves, and no existing required key is retyped. v19 is v18 with one additive amendment (H-194 fine-tuning a generated course): five methods are appended and no existing method, required key, error code, job kind, answer kind, verdict, evidence class or vocabulary value moves. `plan.edit` changes an already-approved plan in place (reorder objectives and/or edit objective title/evidence target/criteria) and records a reviewable `plan_revisions` row; `plan.undo` reverts the last un-reverted structural revision; `lesson.revise` stores one immutable authored revision of one generated section (a new `gen_lessons` row) and marks only that section's validation stale; `lesson.regenerate` queues a single-section lessons job with a one-section cost preflight and never a plan-wide replan; `parent.review.read` returns the pending review diff (plan revisions + lesson revisions) the author approves with the existing `parent.final.approve`. Every mutating method carries `expected_revision` and an `idempotency_key`; `plan.edit` and `lesson.revise` also require the hash the author read, so a stale read is refused rather than applied. The v1-v21 files stay on disk as immutable history. docs/CONTRACTS.md is the authority.

methods.description: Per-method payload contracts. `request` validates envelope.payload; `response` validates envelope.result on success.

level.description: The learner's declared level for this course (for example `L0`). Advisory to the capability policy and the language scaffold; never a grade or a diagnosis. Omitted or null means the brief did not name one.

subject_domain.description: The advisory subject domain (for example `language`, `mathematics`, `repair`). Policy may tighten a media decision with it but can never invent a construct the authored intent did not name. Omitted or null means unknown.

scope.description: How much course the brief asks for: `single` (one lesson), `short` (a bounded few-session course) or `full`. Omitted or null means the brief did not say; it is never inferred from a dial.

presentation_mode.description: The course's mode at creation. `game` records Game intent and opens the World Studio once a draft plan exists; the course reads as Textbook and builds no lessons until both the plan and the world are approved. Omitted means Textbook, and no world job is queued.

acknowledge_prerequisites.description: Proceed past an unmet unit prerequisite after being told which objectives are not independently demonstrated. The acknowledgment is recorded in the response only; it is never evidence, never writes an attempt and never moves an objective.

prerequisite_state.description: Present only when the objective belongs to a unit with prerequisite edges. A legacy or flat plan omits the key (`no_edges` is never invented into the response).

oneOf.description: The validation provenance of the authored page (H-105/H-185/H-194). `independent` is true only for an independently validated page; a model_assessed page is served with `independent: false` and a warning that says the author model assessed its own work, never that a second model did. v19 adds two outcomes: `needs_review` is an authored edit served as text with `check_enabled: false`, and `parent_approved` is an authored edit the course author approved (`check_enabled: true`, still not independent validation). Null when no generation row backs the page (a pack/composed section or a chat-written transcript).

acknowledge_prerequisites.description: Proceed past an unmet unit prerequisite after being told which objectives are not independently demonstrated. The acknowledgment is recorded in the response only; it is never evidence, never writes an attempt and never moves an objective.

prerequisite_state.description: Present only when the objective belongs to a unit with prerequisite edges. A legacy or flat plan omits the key (`no_edges` is never invented into the response).

limit.description: Bound on the objective list; `total` still reports the full count.

request.description: Addressed either by check id (the exact item the pane is showing) or by objective (the open check for the section, else its highest-version check).

kind.description: `hint_request` is the Hint control; `answer_shown` is Show answer. Both are learner actions, never evidence of knowing something.

evidence_class.description: The class the next committed attempt on this objective inherits.

request.description: The five tablet tabs with optional bounds. `sources` is always answered; the four content tabs can be narrowed for a fast paint.

content.description: The re-fetch seam's page text. The backend normalizes whitespace and hashes at most 40000 characters.

oneOf.description: The source was unreachable. It stays historical evidence and is marked `unreachable` for review; no baseline hash is recorded.

evidence_class.description: The full six-label evidence_class vocabulary. The schema accepts every label so that closure is the kernel's policy decision, not a wire enum a client has to reverse-engineer: only `self_reported` and `parent_reported` may be recorded here, and `cold`, `hinted`, `answer_shown` or `override` are refused with POLICY_VIOLATION.

note.description: Optional prose the learner or parent wrote about the observation, stored verbatim in evidence.note (cb.db v9). It is never parsed, graded or exported, and it changes no evidence class: the row stays layer 1, self_reported or parent_reported.

revision.description: The enrollment revision after the write. Recording an observation is an append (no attempt, no transition, no verdict) and it is not gated by expected_revision; the enrollment revision is echoed unchanged because nothing about evidence moves it.

world.read.description: GET-shaped read of the course's durable mode and its latest world. It never generates art and never writes `presentation_mode`; a stored NULL reads as Textbook.

world.style.preview.description: Reads the stored concept boards and the deterministic recommended grammar. No provider call: concept generation is `world.generate(stage=concepts)`.

world.generate.description: Queues one `kind=media` job with `brief.stage` `world_concepts` or `world_kit`. It is never a lesson job; a retry reuses the cache key and never double-spends.

brief_patch.description: Presentation-only edits: mood (`tone`), audience, motifs to include and motifs to avoid. Classification is a course mutation, never a world request.

world.approve.description: Hash-fenced. `stage=style` records the selected concept board as `approved_hash`; `stage=final` accepts the actual kit and freezes the approved hash. It never approves a partial world.

course.mode.set.description: Durable mode switch. `game` without an approved world returns `requires_world=true` and leaves the stored mode unchanged; `textbook` is immediate and hides the world without deleting its assets. A switch never rewrites an objective, check, attempt, evidence row or lesson hash. `expected_revision` is the world revision the caller last read (`world.read.revision`), so a concurrent world change is refused rather than silently overwritten.

sections_done.description: CP-005: objectives of the current plan this enrollment holds independent (or delayed) evidence for. The same fact `evidence_summary.independent` counts; the v3 shelf speaks in sections and never in proofs or a percentage.

sections_total.description: CP-005: objectives in the current plan, the denominator `home.card.meta` names. Zero is an honest empty plan; the read never substitutes a pack's manifest count.

checks_recorded.description: CP-005: distinct checks this enrollment holds a committed attempt for. A pending or failed attempt is not recorded evidence and is not counted.

is_new.description: CP-005: true only when this enrollment has no attempt row at all, which is what the `New` chip may render. Any attempt, committed or not, means the learner has started and the chip is false.

subject_label.description: CP-005: the course's declared subject domain, else null. It is authored text, never derived from the recipe or invented for a badge; the world brief's `unknown_subject` placeholder is never surfaced.

cover_artifact_id.description: CP-005: the approved world's cover artifact, else the pack's declared cover artifact, else null. A rejected, failed or unapproved world never supplies a cover, and the first lesson visual is not a cover.

last_studied_at.description: CP-005: the latest attempt this enrollment recorded (its commit time, else its creation time), else null. Enrollment bookkeeping revisions never move it, and a lesson run a pack import merely prepared is not a study event.

lesson_document.description: The validated lesson document of docs/VISUAL_MEDIA_PLAN.md §5, projected at read time from the durable teaching records. One document serves every view; a view is a lens and may not add a fact. It carries no reference answer, accepted answer or rubric text.

lang.description: Optional text language of the document (H-18). A document projected from a page that recorded a locale carries it; an older page omits it and keeps its old hash. It is the text's language, not a claim about the learner.

direction.description: Optional text direction (H-18). Derived from the text's script, never from a learning-style claim, and it changes no evidence semantics. ltr and rtl render the same blocks.

procedure.description: Optional procedure layout (docs/VISUAL_MEDIA_PLAN.md §8). It is a header over the same blocks: steps are ordered references to this document's blocks plus an optional per-step verification cue, never a second copy of the teaching text and never a second check. Schematic rows are typed facts rendered deterministically; an illustration can never stand in for them.

lesson_procedure_step.description: One numbered step. The action is the referenced block's own authored prose, so a step can never become a second text authority; check is an optional verification cue for that step, not the section check.

lesson_procedure_schematic.description: Typed facts for a deterministic schematic. The renderer draws only these rows; a generated illustration is labelled context and can never carry a torque value, clearance or sequence.

lesson_procedure_source.description: The manual or reference the procedure is taught from, with its permission status. unknown rights are refused, so a technical procedure is never presented beside an unlicensed reference.

lesson_block.description: One structural block. role is where the block sits in the sequence, not a skin. short and deep render the same authored material; short may omit detail but never adds a claim. At most one block in a document carries check_id, and media is always a child of a block.

lesson_document_media.description: Media as a child of a block: one artifact, one purpose, one text equivalent and one honesty label. It is never a free-floating gallery item with no teaching role. A projected legacy segment whose artifact row is unknown is preserved as block text instead, so kind is never guessed.

review_item.description: One derived review item. `due_at` is arithmetic over the declared heuristic ladder, never an attainment prediction; `overdue` and `overdue_days` are computed against the backend clock.

evidence_attempt.description: A committed attempt as the learner may inspect it: their own answer, the criteria that were applied, and the public grading provenance. Never a reference answer, rubric internals or raw grader output.

evidence_event.description: One layer-1 event. `is_action` marks events that are the learner's own statement (hint, shown answer, review action) rather than a graded result.

evidence_l1.description: The raw record: committed attempts and the assist/review events that changed how they count.

evidence_objective.description: The per-objective claim. `independent` is true only when a cold committed pass links here; `attempt_classes` counts how each attempt was produced so a hinted-only objective is visible.

evidence_recommendation.description: A short, revisable recommendation derived from layer 2. It states its basis and never labels the learner; a new kind is a contract bump, not free prose.

evidence_dispute.description: One dispute as first-class record. In cb.db v2 the dispute lives inside the attempt's grading_provenance_json; this shape is the storage-independent view.

evidence_disputes.description: Dispute history for one enrollment. `count` is the full number of matching disputes; `truncated` says whether the bounded `disputes` list omitted any.

pack_list_item.description: One adopted pack identity, read from the local pack library. Identity is pack_id + immutable version; content_hash is the imported manifest's own hash. There is deliberately no filesystem path, no enrollment state and no course id: enrollment facts come from library.list, and the library index is not a second enrollment authority.

source.description: Same enum as cb.db v2 packs.source; a source this build cannot produce is not a contract value.

state.description: Kernel pack state (cb.db v2 packs.state). 'removed' is reserved by the migration and is not produced by this build; 'frozen' is what pack.delete leaves behind, and the content and evidence are still readable.

file_count.description: Files declared by the stored manifest (the manifest itself is not one of them).

expanded_bytes.description: Sum of the declared file sizes; the same figure pack.preview reports in integrity.expanded_bytes.

pack_inspection.description: One installed pack as the library screen and the export review render it: the same identity row pack.list returns, the stored manifest, an integrity block and trust labels. This is pack.preview's payload for a pack that was imported in an earlier session, so an export review never needs a fresh upload.

manifest.description: The stored cb.pack manifest, exactly as imported and re-read from the adopted directory.

hashes_match.description: True only when the recomputed content hash equals the stored manifest_hash and every declared file's size and sha256 match the bytes on disk.

plan_validation.description: H-182/D3 additive amendment: the durable answer to 'may `plan.approve` be pressed for this exact plan version?'. Computed by the same function the command fences on, so a review surface cannot fail open on a rejected or unvalidated draft, and an explicit manual authoring decision (`source: manual`) stays approvable as a human review — never as a validation claim.

outline_plan.description: The plan the outline is the index of: the same plan `library.list` counts an enrollment against (approved preferred, otherwise the highest version). A draft state is what the Plan tab shows the learner to approve; it is not an error.

plan_hash.description: The plan content hash `plan.approve` fences on; null before it is computed.

units.description: Additive unit index of this plan. Absent bytes are never the same as an empty course: a plan with no plan_units row projects one implicit unit on read, and a pack-backed or pre-blueprint plan keeps its flat objective list under that unit.

outline_objective.description: One section of the course as the Textbook and Plan screens render it. Derived, never stored: `check_state` is the highest-version check row for the objective, `attempt_count` is the committed attempts of *this* enrollment on that objective, `independent` is the objective state reaching independent or delayed evidence, `last_opened_at` is the newest lesson run's open time. No reference answer, rubric key, grading provenance or review schedule is derivable here.

check_state.description: `none` when the objective has no check row yet (an approved plan's objective that was never opened, or a draft plan's objective). Otherwise the state of the objective's highest-version check.

independent.description: True only when the objective's own state is independent or delayed evidence.

unit.description: The ordinal of the unit this objective belongs to. Present only when the objective has a non-NULL unit_id; a legacy objective carries no `unit` key and is read as the implicit single unit. `independent` stays the objective's own state.

blueprint_section_identity.description: H-194b: one composed section's identity, served by `parent.blueprint.read` so a fine-tune call can be made on a section that has never been revised. `page_hash` is the exact digest `lesson.revise` fences on (sha256 over the canonical page JSON), so a value read here is accepted by that fence unchanged; it is null exactly when the section has no usable authored page, which is also the case `lesson.revise` refuses and `lesson.regenerate` authors.

check_stimulus.description: The learner-facing question, projectable from `checks.stimulus_json`. Constructed from a closed allowlist of keys; unrecognised stored keys are dropped rather than echoed, so a manifest that smuggled an answer into its stimulus cannot reach the pane through this read.

format.description: How the answer is given. A stored stimulus that declares no format is served as `text`: an imported pack check is an open answer (`cb.projection` v1 emits no format).

items.description: Structured checklist items, projected from `checks.stimulus_json` when the stored stimulus carries them. One label per item is rendered once, on the check surface; a label that repeats another after case, spacing and punctuation are normalised is refused by `check.get` (VALIDATION_FAILED, reason `duplicate_check_item_label`) instead of being served twice. Always present in a served stimulus: an empty array when the check has no items.

learner_instructions.description: Instructions generated with the check, when the stored stimulus carries them.

practice.description: The practice declaration for a conversation practice, projected by domain._stimulus_view from named fields only. `label` is omitted from every target when `targets_visible` is false; a `match` clause, rubric criterion or reference stored beside it is never echoed.

parent_brief.description: The UX_SPEC §10 brief, exactly as the parent wrote it. It is stored in `jobs.brief_json` (the authority the plan executor reads) and read back by `parent.brief.get`, so `duplicate brief` copies real values and never a reconstructed form. No provider, model or credential field exists.

egress_acknowledged.description: The parent saw the provider/egress disclosure before pasting material. A brief that has not acknowledged it is refused by payload validation, before any handler runs, so no course is ever created under an unacknowledged paste.

parent_approval_status.description: The course's final-approval row as the studio renders it. `active` binds one exact content set; `superseded` means an edit invalidated it and the studio must show Changes need review. `plan_hash`/`content_hash` are the hashes that were approved, not the current ones.

parent_export_status.description: Whether `parent.export` would be accepted right now, and the one reason it would not. Derived, never stored: ready is exactly `no_final_approval`, `changes_need_review`, `plan_not_approved` and `no_generated_content` all being absent.

blueprint_file.description: One file of one Parent Studio tab. Declaration-only: the text is the stored bytes for an installed pack file and the generated page/guide/transcript for an authored course. There is no path property, so no filesystem location can cross the wire even by accident; `sha256` and `bytes` are over the declared content, and `truncated` says when the 20000-character served bound clipped it.

parent_reflection.description: One parent-reported reflection. It carries no evidence_class, no verdict and no objective state: a reflection seeds the next draft and never becomes evidence of learning.

name.description: Path inside the exported pack. Relative, no leading slash and no `..` segment; it is a pack-internal name, not a local path.

plan_brief.description: The exact accepted brief for a `plan` job: the same plan-brief inputs `course.create` takes, plus the ids and stage a durable retry needs. Unknown fields are rejected, so a typo cannot silently become an input the policy or planner never reads. Every field is optional because the stage, not this schema, decides when a brief is incomplete (a lesson stage names `plan_id`, an authoring stage names `goal` and `recipe`). The parent-authoring fields are carried because a `parent.brief.create` job is re-queued through `jobs.create` from the brief its own `jobs.get` returned.

budget_usd.description: Optional per-job operator override for the dollar cost ceiling, in USD. Beats COURSEBOOK_JOB_MAX_COST_USD and the plan-sized default; must be positive. Named here because the brief is closed: an unnamed field is refused, and a raised ceiling must stay an accepted, typed brief input.

unit_ordinal.description: The one-based unit ordinal a `unit_sections` authoring job is scoped to. Absent for the plan stage, which authors every unit in one blueprint transaction.

section_id.description: H-194: the one section a `lesson.regenerate` job is scoped to. A lessons job with this field authors only that section at its next gen_lessons version; every other section, its media, checks and progress are untouched.

regenerate.description: H-194: set by `lesson.regenerate` with `section_id`. It forces a new lesson revision instead of reusing the stored version-1 row; absent means the job reuses authored sections as before.

prerequisite_unmet_objective.description: One objective of a prerequisite unit that is not independently demonstrated. It carries the same seven-state label the kernel already stores and nothing derived: no score, probability, readiness number or mastery claim.

prerequisite_state.description: The prerequisite disclosure attached to the two commands that start learner work. `no_edges` is a legacy or flat plan and leaves the command response otherwise unchanged. `satisfied` means every objective of every prerequisite unit is in independent_evidence, delayed_evidence or overridden. `unmet` with acknowledge_prerequisites absent is a PREREQUISITE_UNMET refusal; `unmet_acknowledged` is the same list after the learner accepted it. The acknowledgment is never evidence and never moves an objective.

outline_unit.description: One unit of the current plan as the Textbook and Plan screens render it (blueprint section 14.2 R9). A pre-blueprint plan projects exactly one unit titled with the plan title, with empty prereq_unit_ordinals and prerequisite_state `no_edges`. The key set is frozen: no derived boolean, percentage or 'ready'/'mastered' field may be added.

homework_id.description: A lesson-owned id cited by a homework target (for example `lbl_doa`); content identity, not a Coursebook-minted id.

course_world.description: A course's governed visual kit: textless plates plus a style specification. The renderer composes them with real DOM type and controls.

error.description: The named failure: `reason` plus `missing_roles` when a kit is partial. It never carries a fabricated plate.

world_asset.description: One textless plate of the kit. `role=orientation` is implied by the world contract: this is never an instructional authority.

world_brief.description: The typed brief the backend builds from the approved plan. It has no answer key, check, rubric or attempt field, so the prompt builder cannot leak what it never receives.

route_anchors.description: CP-052: the plate's declared route geometry — where each section sits on the plate box, as normalised 0–1 coordinates. Optional and absent by default: a brief that declares no anchors is unchanged. The renderer falls back to its vertical route when this is absent or empty, and it never invents a coordinate the plate did not declare.

world_route_anchor.description: CP-052: one normalised position of a section on the plate box. `x`/`y` are fractions of the plate's own width/height (0–1, origin top-left), never pixels, so the same plate places the same section at every rendered width. It is geometry only: no label, check, answer key or evidence rides here.

anchor_id.description: Stable id of this anchor within the plate manifest, so a renderer can key a node to it.

section_id.description: The `world_brief.sections[].id` this point belongs to. An anchor never names a section the brief does not declare.

world_concept.description: One textless concept board: a hero crop, a section-card crop and a palette strip as art only. `label` and `medium` are the policy's authored grammar words, never generated text.
